title: Polynomial Interpolation of a Vector Field on a Convex Polyhedral Domain: piecewise polynomial interpolation with tangency and divergence constraints (printed as Proposition 6.2)
author: Junyan Chu, Shizuo Kaji
work: Polynomial Interpolation of a Vector Field on a Convex Polyhedral Domain
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition 6.2 (source0.tex lines 776--778, source label prop:piecewise-interpolation), the criterion for the existence of a piecewise polynomial vector field on a convex polyhedral subdivision that takes prescribed values at prescribed points, is tangent to every exterior facet through those points, and can moreover be chosen divergence-free on every cell. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 779--793 (15 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the three statements it invokes. The proof is a genuine construction: it builds, for each interpolation point, a local polynomial that combines the Lagrange polynomial of the point with the facet equations of the exterior facets and the shared facets of the cells containing it, raising the shared-facet factors to the power that the article's gluing criterion requires, verifies that the resulting pieces have the prescribed values and the required tangency, and then, for the divergence-free case, replaces each piece by the article's lifting operator and checks that the lift preserves the values, the exterior tangency and the gluing order. The substantive steps are the choice of the vanishing factors and the verification that the lift preserves both the tangency and the matching order; neither is an unpacking of definitions. H2: a complete original research-paper proposition, moderately short, whose proof is a genuine construction rather than a routine verification.
